client_brief:
The Marchfield Exchange: Recovered Marchfield crest and engraving geometry

Project overview
The Marchfield Exchange is a listed 1911 commercial building let to law, architecture and accountancy firms. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into Recovered Marchfield crest and engraving geometry, Suite plate run, press file and per suite set, and The Marchfield Exchange small-size geometry evidence sheet.

What we will provide
marchfield_plaque.jpg (5472 x 3648); marchfield_letterhead.jpg (3400 x 4400); marchfield_facade.jpg (6000 x 4000); marchfield_suite_plate_2019.pdf; marchfield_schedule.csv; marchfield_sign_survey.txt. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Scope and deliverables
- Recovered Marchfield crest and engraving geometry: The house crest recovered from physical survivors rather than redrawn, as placeable scalable artwork with a real viewBox and no opaque full canvas path underneath, delivered as the master, a reversed variant for dark ground, and an engraving ready single...
- Suite plate run, press file and per suite set: The 2019 sign shop's press artwork reverse engineered into a live merge template bound to the reconciled schedule, delivered as one press file whose page count equals the reconciled suite count in schedule order, plus per suite named files with identity...
- The Marchfield Exchange small-size geometry evidence sheet: An inspectable proof of Recovered Marchfield crest and engraving geometry at every claimed reproduction size and on light/dark grounds, with open-path, closure, transparency, contour, and unsupported-feature findings stated plainly.

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Recover only features supported by the references; do not describe an automatic trace as engraving, cutting, embroidery, or press ready without inspectable path evidence.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$5,000-$10,000 fixed; target delivery 4 to 6 weeks; direction approval, first-production proof, and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post 'Logo Vectorization + Brand Identity Kit' (cands/cand_45.json, db_i 0), whose client has 'an existing logo I love' and needs a designer to 'Vectorize and clean up my current logo to print-ready quality' and 'Build out a full set of logo variations and brand files I can use across everything', listing 'Master logo in vector format', a 'One-color version (white on dark, black on light)' and files 'sized and ready for' named physical applications, and stating 'Please do NOT apply if: You only deliver JPG or PNG files'. Co-anchor: the Upwork post 'Logo Design & Challenge Coin Artwork' (cands/cand_38.json, db_i 95), which asks for artwork 'that can be sent to a mint/manufacturer', insists on 'True vector artwork, not raster images' and requires it be 'Readable at small sizes'. Neither post names a real client; the managing agent, the building, its crest and its tenants are invented here. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the first post's 'exact hex, CMYK, and Pantone codes' and 'Font identification' are not connector work, since nothing here measures a colour or identifies a typeface from an image, so the commission is carried by what is real: recovery of a mark surviving only on physical objects, engraving ready geometry judged against a fabricator's stated minimum stroke, panels authored at true physical sizes as a native editable document, and a per suite plate run built off the previous sign shop's own press artwork.

Neither post names a real client; the managing agent, the building, its crest and its tenants are invented here. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the first post's 'exact hex, CMYK, and Pantone codes' and 'Font identification' are not connector work, since nothing here measures a colour or identifies a typeface from an image, so the commission is carried by what is real: recovery of a mark surviving only on physical objects, engraving ready geometry judged against a fabricator's stated minimum stroke, panels authored at true physical sizes as a native editable document, and a per suite plate run built off the previous sign shop's own press artwork.
price_band_and_audience: A listed heritage building letting at forty five to seventy five dollars per square foot to law, architecture and accountancy firms, with a board approving the spend. At this tier the programme is engraved brass and stone appropriate metalwork, a serif with real heritage credibility, deep margins, generous clear space around the crest, and a directory that reads as a document rather than as signage. Push down into a budget system and it becomes moulded plastic, a condensed grotesque, tight margins and a loud contrast board, which at this rent reads as neglect and undermines the one asset the tenants pay for. Push up into contemporary luxury and it becomes a minimal sans on a dark monolith, which fights a 1911 stone entrance and reads as a refurbishment a conservation officer would refuse. Either extreme misreads the commission even where every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 4,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: A listed 1911 commercial building, managed by a property agent, let as office suites to professional firms, with a heritage sign programme.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Building completed 1911 in Portland, Maine. Fourteen lettable suites, overseen by a managing agent and a building board.
brand_identity.about: The Marchfield Exchange is a listed 1911 commercial building let to law, architecture and accountancy firms. The building itself, its stone entrance and brass fittings, is the reason tenants take space here. Its house crest is original to 1911, and the sign programme is being rebuilt as one coherent system that respects the building's character.
brand_identity.audience: Professional firms choosing a building with a stone entrance and brass fittings, and a building board approving the spend. Tenants who read signage as a signal of how the building is kept.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A listed heritage building letting at 45 to 75 dollars per square foot. The programme is engraved brass and stone appropriate metalwork, deep margins and generous clear space. Anything that would look at home on a retail park reads as neglect at this rent.
brand_identity.typography: A heritage serif with real credibility carries the building name and the crest lockup. A quieter companion serif or restrained roman sets the directory and suite plates, so the board reads as a document rather than as signage.
brand_identity.voice: Formal, measured, understated. A line the agent would write: "The Marchfield Exchange. Established 1911. Professional suites in the heart of the city."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No drawing, plate or digital file of the crest exists, and the original architect's practice closed in 1961. The crest survives in exactly two places: engraved on the weathered brass entry plaque, photographed on the wall, and printed on a 1950s tenant letterhead, scanned. The suite plates survive only as the 2019 sign shop's single press PDF.
brand_identity.values: The building's history is the asset, so the crest is recovered rather than reinvented, and the programme is kept editable so the agent can update a tenant name without a designer.

assets_supplied.name: marchfield_plaque.jpg (5472 x 3648)
assets_supplied.kind: The original engraved brass entry plaque photographed on the facade in late afternoon raking light, handheld, the crest filling most of the frame.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The plaque by the door. This is the crest, on the real thing."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The polished bevel throws a specular ridge sitting brighter than the engraved field, so a graphic level selection takes the ridge as if it were part of the crest, while along the shaded left third the incised line and the brass run to nearly the same value and the wreath does not come back there at all. Neither is apparent on the photograph, which reads as the sharper and more authoritative of the two sources.

assets_supplied.name: marchfield_letterhead.jpg (3400 x 4400)
assets_supplied.kind: A flatbed scan of a 1950s tenant letterhead carrying the same crest at about thirty millimetres, one deep ink on cream stock, the sheet foxed at the edges.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "A letterhead a tenant found in a filing cabinet. Same crest, much smaller."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: At the size it was printed the ink gained, so two of the crest's interior rules have run into one another and the ribbon's counters have filled, a closure invisible on the sheet and obvious only beside the other candidate. The crest also occupies a small part of a large scan, so what looks like a high resolution source is a small source inside a big file, and nothing downstream may enlarge it.

assets_supplied.name: marchfield_facade.jpg (6000 x 4000)
assets_supplied.kind: A photograph of the entrance bay taken for the board's approval mockup, the existing plaque in place in a shaded stone reveal.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The entrance, so we can see the new plaque where it will actually go."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: In the shaded reveal the limestone surround and the brass plaque field run to nearly the same value along the left edge, so an automatic isolation of the plaque area reports success, previews convincingly and bites that edge, leaving a crescent of the old engraving and a ragged stone boundary that appears only at full resolution.

assets_supplied.name: marchfield_suite_plate_2019.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The previous sign shop's print ready artwork for a single suite plate from the 2019 refit, a genuine press PDF at plate trim, one ink.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The plate artwork from the last refit. It is the only file the old sign shop left us."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The suite number and the firm name look like two separate blocks on the page and are one continuous run in the file, so fields have to be reached by position inside a single story rather than frame by frame. It also carries the abandoned 2019 numbering convention in its own text, which no longer matches the schedule, and no bleed can be introduced into anything derived from it.

assets_supplied.name: marchfield_schedule.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The managing agent's current tenant schedule: suite number, floor, firm name and lease status, in the order the directory board is to read.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our current schedule. Fourteen suites, in the order we want them on the board."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two suites appear twice, once under their 2019 number and once under the number in use since the renumbering, so the row count is not the suite count. One suite is vacant with an empty firm cell, which merges into a plate carrying a blank line rather than being skipped, and three firm names carry an ampersand while one runs to thirty eight characters.

assets_supplied.name: marchfield_sign_survey.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The fabricator's site survey as plain text: entrance sign, directory board and suite plate sizes in millimetres, substrate and fixing for each, and the shop's minimum engraved stroke width at final size.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What our fabricator measured and what his machine can hold."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which of the two surviving records of the crest is usable, and the answer is that neither is usable whole. The plaque photograph is larger, sharper and the real object, but the raking light's specular ridge along the bevel traces as if it were geometry and the shaded left third gives no separation at all, so the wreath is simply absent there. The letterhead is even and complete but was printed small, so the ink gained until two interior rules merged and the ribbon's counters filled, a closure invisible on the sheet that declares itself only beside the other trace at suite plate size. Both traces succeed, both look convincing at canvas scale, and the failures are in different places on each.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not avoid it, and tracing both is competent practice rather than a dodge, because what cannot be known in advance is where each source fails, which is a property of this light on this metal and this ink on this stock. The tracer has no parameters at all. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the crest survives in two places and must come back as the building's crest. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different chain: a confined correction over the shaded third to open a separation that does not yet exist, a re-worded selection at incised level, a re-trace, and a fresh comparison at the same reproduction sizes.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the raster stage on the chosen capture, lift the shaded region with a confined correction rather than a whole frame move, re-select and re-trace, and judge the result again at the smallest reproduction size on brass before anything downstream is built on it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A heritage crest shipped to a brass engraver with a specular ridge cut into it as if it were part of the design, or with a wreath that stops a third of the way round, permanently, on a listed building's entrance.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the treatment the whole programme's look rests on. An incised, engraved register is reached in an authored page by exactly the constructions this importer quietly discards: a blur filter is dropped outright, a layered shadow is truncated to its first layer, a text shadow is dropped, an outline is dropped, and a stroked letterform written with a text stroke and a transparent fill comes back fully invisible rather than as an outline. Every one of those returns success with no warning. The document's own rendition shows the first panel only, so the entrance sign may look right while the directory board and the plate sheet have lost the treatment entirely, and the returned per panel markup is the only channel that reports it.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time would mean knowing in advance which of several equally reasonable constructions survives, which nothing reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a quiet traditional register and for panels the agent can edit later. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different construction: the incised register rebuilt from what does survive, real strokes on shapes, a single shadow layer, borders and gradients, or carried up into the raster stage so the treatment is part of the artwork rather than a page effect, then a re-author and a fresh audit of every panel.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the incised treatment from constructions the importer keeps, re-author the HTML around that decision, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every panel from the returned markup rather than from the first one.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A sign programme approved by a building's board on the strength of the one panel anybody looked at, with the directory board and the plate sheet arriving flat, and in the worst case a panel whose lettering is present in the document and invisible on the canvas.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the plaque field in the facade photograph can be isolated cleanly at all. In the shaded reveal the limestone surround and the brass run to nearly the same value along the left edge, and an automatic isolation there returns a result that reports success, previews convincingly at the scale anyone would check it at, and bites that edge, so a crescent of the old engraving survives inside the supposedly cleared field and the stone boundary comes back ragged. Where it bites, and how far, is a property of this bay in this light and appears only at full resolution.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because the tool has no edge tolerance to set and the failure is in the material rather than in the call. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks only to see the new plaque on the building before the board commits. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different chain: select the limestone as a material by its own surface properties, invert that selection, and drive the fill from the ground instead of from the object, a route the naive attempt never touches.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the object led isolation, select the surrounding stone as a material, invert it, fill from that mask, and inspect the boundary at full resolution rather than at preview scale before the mockup panel is authored around it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An approval mockup in which the old engraving is still faintly visible under the new plaque and the stone edge is chewed, put in front of a building's board as the thing they are asked to sign off.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are authored panels at fixed physical sizes and which is a genuine record per page run, given that only one surface here composes free form layout.
Which surviving record of the crest is the master, when the more authoritative looking capture is not necessarily the more even one and the answer may be neither on its own.
How much of the crest's detail survives at suite plate size, and whether a simplified interpretation is needed below a stated size or whether one drawing serves every panel.
How to produce true interior holes, given that background removal fills an enclosed interior and returns something that looks correct until it sits on a colour.
What the fabricator's minimum stroke means per panel, since a hairline that is fine on an entrance sign can be unroutable on a plate.
How to reconcile a tenant schedule the client believes is the suite list, given a renumbering that left duplicates and a vacant suite that would otherwise print a plate with a hole in it.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a listed 1911 building at forty five to seventy five dollars a square foot rather than against a signage category.
How to deliver identity safely across fourteen plates, since files named by their position in a response are not files named by whose door they go on.

The sign document is editable by the managing agent next season: live retypeable text, the crest as real vector shapes, and the source it was built from delivered alongside.
Production-readiness claims are limited to geometry that can be inspected; vectorization alone is never accepted as evidence of fabrication readiness.

The engraving artwork is a single closed outline with counters present as true holes, a real viewBox, and no opaque field underneath. Artwork that looks correct on screen and routes solid on the machine fails.
Every supplied asset is listed in the delivery manifest as used, reference-only, superseded, or rejected with a concrete reason; no input disappears silently.
Final files open successfully, use unambiguous names, match the stated dimensions and formats, and include editable sources only where the scoped deliverable requires them.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome heraldic crest and pictures of signs. IDENTITY: this is a specific 1911 building's own crest, surviving on two physical objects, and a regenerated crest is a different building's history, which is exactly what a listed building's board is paying not to receive. SPEC: the fabricator engraves from geometry, so the deliverable is a closed outline with true interior holes whose every stroke clears his machine's stated minimum at each panel's real size, and the plates are a page per suite in the agent's own schedule order carrying real tenant names at press resolution at trim, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the whole point of the handover is that the agent changes a tenant name themselves when a lease turns over, so the directory has to be live cells and the plate template has to be re-runnable. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: which capture holds where, whether this counter is still a hole at plate size, whether the isolation bit the stone, whether the treatment survived on the panels nobody previewed.

proof: Every required operation is present in the captured 99-tool ChatGPT Adobe inventory.
The client brief is host-neutral; connector-specific scoring is isolated in connector_profile and verifier_contract.
Artifact acceptance never depends on a raw connector response field.
Unsupported truth, fabrication, press, legal, or color claims have an explicit defer or disclose state.
residual_limits: Express work is template adaptation, not unrestricted canvas authoring.
Quick Cut is used only for visually led selection and never as semantic speech editing.
Automatic vectorization does not independently establish fabrication readiness.
Interactive Acrobat page-organization operations are excluded from zero-human execution.
